title: Reaction Motors XLR99
note: The X-15's rocket engine (Thiokol's Reaction Motors Division), as displayed at the National Museum of the USAF. Frame: thrust axis z up, the nozzle exit (the hoop round it) at z = 0; +x is up in photo_usaf (the side of the engine-mount truss's single top fitting), +y away from that photo's camera (its near side is -y).

propellants.value: liquid oxygen and anhydrous ammonia; the turbopump driven by 90% hydrogen peroxide
propellants.quote: Engine - liquid oxygen and ammonia; Pump - 90 percent hydrogen peroxide

thrust_lbf.conflict: nasm_xlr99: "Rated at 50,000 lb thrust" in its summary, "60,000lb thrust" in its physical description

throttle.quote: variable thrust over a continuous range from 50 percent to 100 percent of rated thrust

single_chamber.quote: has a single thrust chamber, injector, gas generator, two-stage ignitor, turbo-pump, and variable governor control, and lime green thrust mounts

turbopump.value: one turbine driving both pumps; exhausts into the thrust chamber
turbopump.quote: A two-stage impulse turbine drove the single-inlet oxidizer pump and two-inlet fuel pump. The hydrogen-peroxide-driven turbopump exhausted into the thrust chamber.

mount.value: rigid truss, three fittings on the fuselage; not gimballed
mount.quote: they designed a rigid engine mount without any special vibration attenuation. The engine-mount truss attached to the fuselage at three fittings, and by adjusting the lower two fittings the engineers could tailor the thrust vector of the engine.

nozzle_tubes.quote: a brazed assembly of 547 stainless steel tubes, formed to shape, through which the anhydrous ammonia flows longitudinally as a coolant

open_questions: Overall length: built 1.92 m (75 in) from photo_usaf, flange to the exit ring. Jenkins (p.198) gives the 1956 proposal's envelope as 71.7 in long and 43.2 in across; Wikipedia's infobox gives 82 in, citing Wilkinson's Aircraft Engines of the World 1964/65 (not read); nasm_xlr99 lists unlabelled sizes 40 1/4 x 87 x 56 x 95 x 48 in (with its stand). The photo's perspective may shorten the front end.
Exit diameter 0.69 m outside (27 in) from the photo; a dealer's page for a spare nozzle body says 30 in (weak source, not used).

The +y side comes from photo_nasm (a different engine, the Smithsonian's, which its catalogue says is missing a fuel pump): its long duct and teardrop housing are built there; their depth isn't seen in any photo. Neither side's dense small plumbing is modelled, only the larger lines.
Colours from one museum photo under warm light, white-balanced on the white exhaust duct.
The NASM engine's front end has red-capped fittings out to about z 2.0 instead of the USAF engine's white duct (z 1.9); the model follows the USAF engine.
